title: Canonical filtered density of ordinary presentable objects
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small. Let $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal and let $\mathcal A$ be a locally small ordinary category in $\mathcal U'$ with all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A category is $\lambda$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms has a cocone; an object $a$ is $\lambda$-presentable if $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(a,-)$ preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is locally $\lambda$-presentable, meaning that every object is a small $\lambda$-filtered colimit of objects from a fixed small family of $\lambda$-presentable objects. Let $\mathcal P_\lambda\subseteq\mathcal A$ be the full subcategory of all $\lambda$-presentable objects. Then $\mathcal P_\lambda$ is essentially small (equivalent to a small category). For every $X\in\mathcal A$, the comma category $(\mathcal P_\lambda\downarrow X)$, whose objects are maps $u:a\to X$ with $a\in\mathcal P_\lambda$ and whose arrows $t:a\to a'$ satisfy $u't=u$, is $\lambda$-filtered. The canonical cocone with components $u$ on the value diagram $(a,u)\mapsto a$ is colimiting; equivalently, its canonical comparison from the colimit to $X$ is an isomorphism. Colimits over an essentially small category mean colimits after passage to a small equivalent category.
